answer: Isolating every agent inside a dedicated network island prevents contaminated data from flowing upstream. Just as a physical reef traps debris before it chokes the main intake, a cryptographic proof-of-work barrier filters out unauthorized fake identities. Building this computational wall drains the attackers literal processing power through a costly verification vine. The economic limitation is that well-funded adversaries can still brute-force entries if hardware subsidies outpace power expenditure rates.
